subject: seal
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: seal, in the place of the game's models/player/seal/seal.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/player/agent/agent.mdl, models/player/terrorist/terrorist.mdl, models/player/castor/castor.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 3 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, C, B where the asset was C, D, A: passed for one of the game's
measured.contract: keeps the contract the mod's stock players share: their animations at their numbers, their shared bones, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (an upright special forces operator in fatigues, a dark vest with pouches, boots, gloves, balaclava), every view reads as that figure: the balaclava head, the vest's chest pouches and back, the tan trousers and knee pads, the boots, the gloves. Side and back views show the same outline. Nothing sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: Measured height 70.1 against the brief's 70 (0.1% off), within 15%. Width 23.9 and depth 24.5 are human-scale, with no size given in the brief to compare them with.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, down to the small ones: balaclava with eye openings, dark vest with chest and side pouches (front and back views), elbow and knee pads, belt, two boots with laces, two black gloves with fingers, tan fatigue trousers and jacket. All are present, one of each where a person has one. Pouches are cut into the vest's front rather than modelled separately, but they read clearly at the size the game shows.

M4.reason: Tan fatigues, a black vest, black gloves and a black balaclava: each region reads as its material (cloth, leather-like vest, gloves). Paint looks the same across the views with no region off in colour.

M5.reason: Surface detail is present and at a sensible sharpness: a silver emblem on the back of the vest, chest pouch flaps and zip, seams on the fatigues, lacing on the boots, and knee-pad straps. The brief asks for none of these in particular, and none contradicts it.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up measure. In the line-up the asset (D) stands beside three Valve models and reads as one of them, in material, posture and detail, and the three judges' picks were each wrong. The line-up test is measured apart and not scored by this judge.

M7.reason: Front view faces forward, upright, feet flat on the floor line. Front and back views show the same figure, so the front is clearly the front.

M8.reason: 2617 triangles, which equals the most Valve spends on a model of this kind and size (half-life most: 2617), so it is not past the limit. Nothing visible is left open or floating in the views given. SMAK's check passes per the measurements.

C1.reason: Run cycle (30 frames): arms and legs swing and the vest, head and hands stay attached through every frame, with no part sinking or floating. Attack (shoot_onehanded, 20 frames): the figure leans and keeps its parts together. Stunt (dive_f_akimbo, 35 frames): the body goes horizontal and extends cleanly, with the arms and legs trailing as the original's dive does. Nothing comes apart.

C2.reason: The measured contract is kept: its bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts are the canonical player's (compareContract is recorded as kept, with no fault reported). The stunt and run play on the stock animations.
